# Riverbend Nonprofit Network theory of change: assessment

## Summary

This draft has 22 outcomes (20 within the organization's accountability), 10 interventions, 12 assumptions, and 27 indicators, organized into 3 pathway(s). Of its 123 elements, 20 are stated by cited sources, 48 are our inference or hypothesis, 22 are confirmed by the organization, and 33 have no basis recorded. The inferred and hypothesis elements are the first to check with the organization.

## Where each element comes from

| Basis | Meaning | Elements |
|-------|---------|----------|
| Stated | A cited source says it | 20 |
| Inferred | Our reading of the sources | 27 |
| Hypothesis | A guess to test | 21 |
| Confirmed | The organization agreed to it | 22 |
| Rejected | Considered and set aside | 4 |
| No basis recorded | — | 33 |

| Internal new | Leadership practice maturity; Member collaboration maturity; Back-office share of operating budget; Grant applications submitted by members using the calendar; Members with three or more distinct funding sources; Cohort attendance rate; Stories of members helping each other |
| Partner held | Level of members' voice with local government and funders; Public planning processes that invited members |
| Unknown | Residents served by member organizations |

### Assumptions needing testing

- Member leaders can free enough time to attend cohort sessions and coaching. (`asm-time-to-attend`): Track the share of enrolled leaders who attend at least three quarters of sessions, and ask drop-outs why they left.
- Leaders put coaching-based skills into practice back at their organizations. (`asm-skills-applied`): Interview a sample of cohort graduates six months later and score their practice with the maturity rubric.
- Vendors offer meaningful discounts and service terms at the volume the members can pool. (`asm-vendor-terms`): Compare pooled vendor quotes with the prices a sample of members pay now, before signing each agreement.
- The county planning office and municipal councils stay open to a standing channel with the network. (`asm-officials-receptive`): Review the county planning calendar each quarter for processes that invited members, and ask planning staff whether the channel was used.
- Once members adopt a joint position, they keep to it in public rather than splintering. (`asm-positions-hold`): After each joint position, record whether any member publicly took a conflicting stance within the following quarter.
- Stronger, more connected, better-funded members deliver more and better services to residents. (`asm-members-deliver`): Compare service volumes and waits at members with high and low maturity ratings, using the annual member service-count report.

### Open decisions

- Should the network hire a part-time civic liaison for the county channel? (`dec-liaison-staff`). Options: Hire part-time; Share a role with Shared Services; Rely on the steering group
- Should pooled services move from free trial to member fees in 2027? (`dec-service-fees`). Options: Introduce sliding fees; Keep free through 2027; Fee only large members
